quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The coach said, 'If she had practised more, she would have performed better.'
options: The coach said that if she had practised more, she would have performed better.
The coach said that if she practised more, she would perform better.
The coach said that if she had practised more, she would perform better.

quests.sentence: The coach said, 'If she had practised more, she would have performed better.'
quests.hint: Third conditional: 'had practised' and 'would have performed' are already past perfect and conditional perfect. They stay unchanged.
quests.explanation: Third conditional structures ('had practised / would have performed') cannot shift further back and remain unchanged in reported speech.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: She asked, 'Do you ever wish you had made different choices?'

quests.sentence: She asked, 'Do you ever wish you had made different choices?'
quests.hint: 'Wish' → 'wished'. 'Had made' stays (already past perfect). 'You' → 'I'. Use 'if'.
quests.explanation: 'Wish' → 'wished'. 'Had made' is already past perfect - it stays. 'You' → 'I'. Use 'if' and statement word order.

quests.hint: Imperative: 'advised + users + to + back up'. 'Your' → 'their'.
quests.explanation: 'Back up' is an imperative → 'advised users to back up'. 'Your data' → 'their data'.

quests.hint: 'Needn't have worried' stays (past modal perfect). 'Turned out' → 'had turned out'.
quests.explanation: 'Needn't have worried' is a past modal perfect - it stays unchanged. 'Turned out' shifts to 'had turned out'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: He asked, 'What would have happened if we hadn't intervened?'

quests.explanation: Third conditional: both 'would have happened' and 'hadn't intervened' are already past - they stay unchanged. 'We' → 'they'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The teacher said, 'Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius.'

quests.hint: Universal scientific truth: the present tense is retained in reported speech.
quests.explanation: Scientific and universal truths are reported without tense shift. 'Boils' stays as 'boils'. Note: 'told' requires an object - 'said' is correct.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The admissions officer asked, 'Why did you choose this university over others?'

quests.sentence: The admissions officer asked, 'Why did you choose this university over others?'
quests.hint: 'Did choose' → 'had chosen'. 'You' → 'I'. 'This' → 'that'. Statement order.
quests.explanation: Drop 'did'. 'Choose' → 'had chosen'. 'You' → 'I'. 'This university' → 'that university'. Use statement word order.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The life coach said, 'Challenge yourself to step outside your comfort zone every day.'

quests.hint: Reflexive imperative: 'urged + us + to + challenge ourselves'. Pronouns shift throughout.
quests.explanation: 'Challenge yourself' → 'to challenge ourselves'. 'Your comfort zone' → 'our comfort zones'. Reflexive pronoun 'yourself' → 'ourselves'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The expert was asked, 'What are the long-term implications of this policy?'

quests.explanation: 'Are' → 'were'. 'This' → 'that'. Statement word order: 'what the implications... were', not 'what were the implications'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The career guide said, 'Invest in your professional development every year.'

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: He said, 'I didn't break the window!'
options: He denied breaking the window.

He denied that he didn't break the window.

quests.hint: 'Deny' is followed by a gerund (-ing form), not an infinitive.
quests.explanation: 'Deny' must be followed by the gerund form: 'denied breaking'. 'Denied to break' is grammatically incorrect. Option C creates a double negative.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: She said, 'I suggest we take a different route to avoid the traffic.'

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The CEO asked, 'Why is the production running below capacity?'

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: She said, 'Don't make promises you can't keep.'
